scopeNotes.covers: Stage 3B covers the text daily cycle, personal context, safe aggregates, employee weekly/final reporting, minimal automation map seed, privacy backbone behavior, schema-linked contracts, CLI-driven executable specs, Mastra wrappers, and generated traceability.
scopeNotes.outOfScope: Out of scope remains real Telegram delivery, real methodologist web panel, real LLM/STT provider calls, and production-grade database/encryption/KMS.

productParts.title: Privacy, consent, and methodologist boundary layer.
Reporting and automation map contour: signal candidates, safe aggregates, future reports.

userStories.story: As a methodologist, I can create a program flow and generate an employee invite.
acceptance: A methodologist creates a flow with client name and date range.
A methodologist generates an invite token for an employee role.

userStories.story: As an employee, I can open an invite, accept consent, and complete onboarding.
acceptance: The employee opens the invite and is connected to the flow.
The employee accepts a privacy version before personal context is created.
Completing onboarding emits `ParticipantOnboarded`.

userStories.story: As an employee, I receive a soft refusal when I ask Minutka to produce out-of-scope work output.
acceptance: A work-output request is rejected by the selected work-scope boundary process.
The response redirects the employee back to learning and reflection.
No final work product is generated or exposed to the methodologist.

userStories.story: As a methodologist, I see only safe aggregate signals for groups of at least 5 participants.
acceptance: Aggregates for 5+ participants are visible.
Aggregates for 1-4 participants are hidden.
Raw messages and personal profile fields are never returned.

userStories.story: As an employee, I can delete my personal context and message history without asking the company.
acceptance: The employee requests deletion through the CLI/API.
Personal context and message history disappear.
Safe non-identifying aggregates and audit events follow policy.

userStories.story: As a methodologist, I see operational engagement labels without access to message content.
acceptance: After 2 missed days status is `lagging`.
After 3 or more missed days status is `dropped_off`.
Message content, emotion and productivity do not influence the label.

userStories.story: As a methodologist, I can initiate a soft reminder based on engagement state without seeing private messages.
acceptance: The methodologist can request a reminder for `lagging` or `dropped_off` participants.
The reminder request payload contains no private content.
Telegram delivery remains out of scope.

userStories.story: As an employee, I submit a morning text plan and receive a structured day plan without productivity scoring.
acceptance: The morning plan is saved in employee-private daily context.
The response structures priorities and constraints without productivity or performance scoring.
The methodologist participant view cannot expose the plan text.

userStories.story: As an employee, I submit a midday check-in and receive a soft adjustment to the current plan.
acceptance: The midday check-in links to the same program day and morning plan when one exists.
The response suggests a practical, non-judgmental adjustment.
Daily content and emotional state stay out of the methodologist contour.

userStories.story: As an employee, I submit an evening text reflection that updates my private context and prepares safe aggregate signal candidates.
acceptance: Evening text creates private personal observation proposals.
Evening text creates structured business-signal candidates without raw transcript.
Methodologist/client views cannot see the message content or individual emotional state.

userStories.story: As an employee, I can inspect and correct my personal context in the "Me" area.
acceptance: The employee can read, correct, reject and delete personal observations.
Corrected context affects the next daily response.
Other employees and methodologist/client contours cannot access the private context.

userStories.story: As an employee, I receive a weekly summary and confirm or reject proposed personal patterns.
acceptance: The weekly summary uses cautious language and asks for confirmation.
The employee confirms or rejects patterns through explicit requester identity.
Rejected observations or patterns are not treated as confirmed facts.

userStories.story: As an employee, I receive a final personal report that remains private to me.
acceptance: The final report is generated only for an explicitly matching employee requester.
The report does not compare the employee with peers or score performance.
Methodologist/client contours cannot fetch the personal report, and deleted or rejected facts are excluded.

userStories.story: As a methodologist, I prepare a minimal automation map draft from safe aggregate signals.
acceptance: The draft uses only safe aggregates and hides groups below 5.
Automation map operations require explicit methodologist identity and role.
The methodologist can edit narrative without seeing raw personal data.

requirements.statement: The system must let a methodologist create a program flow and invite a participant.
The system must let an employee start onboarding, accept consent, and complete onboarding.
The runtime must classify and refuse out-of-scope work-output requests before content generation.
The system must not create personal context before consent is accepted.
The methodologist must not access transcript, personal profile, message content, or emotional state.

Provider calls must require privacy-boundary preparation. Structured data uses safe projections; free-text payloads are masked or excluded before any agent/provider path. Stage 1 uses fake deterministic provider behavior, but the runtime keeps the policy gate in front of any agent/provider path.
The system prepares safe aggregate signals for the methodologist/client contour.
The employee can request deletion of personal context and message history.
The methodologist can see activity-derived participation labels.
The methodologist can request a soft reminder for a participant using safe engagement state.
Privacy-sensitive actions create audit events without raw private content.
Groups with fewer than 5 participants are hidden from the methodologist/client contour.
Personal context and message history are deleted after an employee request.
Already-created anonymized aggregates may remain only if they cannot identify the employee.
Engagement labels are based only on missed-day counts, not content, emotion or productivity evaluation.

Free-text PII such as full names, phone numbers and common contact/network identifiers is masked or excluded before external provider calls. Structured fields are protected by schema-aware privacy projections rather than generic PII scanning.
Reminder requests use engagement state and operational identifiers, not transcript, profile, emotional state or productivity inference.
Aggregate signals and methodologist/client responses pass privacy output checks before persistence or return.
Audit logs record sensitive actions without storing raw transcript or personal profile.
The system captures text daily interactions with kind `morning`, `midday` or `evening_text`.
The system captures morning plan priorities, constraints and accepted plan state.
The system compares a midday check-in with the morning plan when available and proposes a safe adjustment.
The system captures evening text reflection, creates personal observations and prepares aggregate candidates.
The employee can read and correct personal context used by future responses.
The runtime extracts structured candidate signals from daily context before anonymization/aggregation.
Daily responses must not score employee productivity or performance.
Personal context is readable/editable by the same employee and AI runtime only, not by other employees or methodologist/client contours.
Signal candidates cannot store raw transcript, exact personal task text, full name, phone or personal profile fields.
The Stage 2 deletion path covers Stage 3A daily context, personal observations, private message history if stored and signal candidates.
The system generates employee reports with `kind: weekly | final`.
The weekly summary proposes cautious personal patterns and records employee review decisions.
The final personal report is generated from employee-private context and history for employee access only.
The automation map seed is prepared from safe aggregate report data.
The methodologist can edit automation map narrative without accessing raw personal data.
Employee report operations require explicit requester/target binding and cannot default requester identity to the target employee.
Proposed weekly patterns are not treated as confirmed facts until employee review.
Final personal reports are never exposed to methodologist/client APIs.
Automation map output uses only safe aggregates and methodologist-authored narrative.
Automation map operations require methodologist role/identity binding and cannot be called through employee-private DTOs.
Automation map output cannot include raw transcript, exact personal task, personal profile, full name, phone or individual emotional state.
Deleted or rejected personal observations cannot reappear as confirmed facts in employee reports.
